verdict.rationale: cubic documents a repo-root `cubic.yaml` that is the source of truth for AI review behavior and custom agents. Custom agents are review rules that enforce an organization's coding standards and best practices, and an org-wide `cubic-config` repo can supply defaults for repositories without their own file. Missing for 10: detail on the file's instruction syntax or support for free-form convention guidance (beyond review rules), and independent or hands-on corroboration that the agent follows these rules.

support.subject: As a developer, I can add a project instructions file to set coding standards and conventions the agent follows

citations.quote: `cubic.yaml` lives in the root of your repository and becomes the source of truth for AI review behavior, ignore patterns, PR descriptions, and custom agents.
Custom agents are review rules that enforce your organization's specific best practices across pull requests.
**Custom agents**: Enforce your team’s coding standards
cubic automatically applies these settings to any repository that doesn't have its own configuration.
